questions.question: Defend the claim that mining is the foundation of the modern South African economy while conceding its current size.
questions.expected_answer: Concede the numbers: mining earns under ten per cent of GDP directly and employs under half a million people. Then the foundation case: railways were driven inland to serve Kimberley and the Witwatersrand, the coal-fired power system grew to supply the mines, the JSE was created to fund the goldfields, manufacturing and banking grew as mining's suppliers, and Johannesburg itself exists because of gold. Mining still anchors export earnings (platinum group metals, coal, iron ore, gold), pays royalties and taxes, and supports towns and multiplier jobs — the house was built on it even though other floors now earn more.

questions.question: Describe where South Africa's platinum is mined and the factors favouring the industry.
questions.expected_answer: In the Bushveld Igneous Complex, a vast layered igneous saucer under the northern interior, mined along three limbs — western (Rustenburg/Brits in North West), eastern (Burgersfort/Steelpoort) and northern (Mokopane) — following the thin Merensky Reef and UG2 chromitite layer. Favouring factors: exceptionally large, high-grade, predictable reserves; a century of deep-mining expertise inherited from gold; proximity to Gauteng's rail, power, water and skills; an established mining workforce; and sustained world demand for autocatalysts, jewellery and hydrogen fuel cells.

questions.question: Explain how mining activity is identified on a topographic map and how the evidence should be written up.
questions.expected_answer: Signs: the printed words Mine/Myn/Colliery/Quarry; pale, straight-edged mine dumps and rectangular slimes dams (shapes nature does not build); toothed or hachured excavation symbols; a railway spur or heavy road dead-ending at a building cluster in open country; power lines converging on one site; and a grid-planned town beside the workings. Write each piece as feature, map appearance and grid reference — eastings before northings, along the corridor then up the stairs.
